Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with `README.md`, then I’ll apply the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this is a multi-wake dogfish policy change. I’ll inspect the required rollout keyframes before touching `solver/`, then update the candidate, policy notes, and reusable control lesson together.

The skill requires a visual-first comparison before any policy edit. I’ll now anchor the keyframes to the guidance, observations, metrics, diagnostics, inherited optimizer logs, and the current candidate; the three top examples are numerically identical, so I’ll treat one as the best representative and compare it with the lower-scoring `solver_31ed…` example unless the inherited logs reveal a more informative failure.

The evidence shows a real local negative result, not a semantic crash: gain `1.9` and inherited `1.725` both preserve the route but worsen arrival, distance, crossflow, loads, power, and joint excursions relative to the replicated `1.7` anchor. Per the skill, I’m now inspecting the shared prewarm first, then the `1.7`, `1.9`, and `1.725` released sheets to verify that the metrics reflect the same visible trajectory class.

The images confirm the policies are self-propelled and share the same early turn and diagonal wake-entry topology; the worse candidates are not failures of route choice but produce a flatter, more load-heavy approach. The three sampled `1.7` rollouts are exact deterministic replicas, satisfying the inherited repeat boundary. I’ll now use the exposed task-state contract to choose one separately bounded feedback axis, without importing any omitted shelf or changing the proven propulsion/curvature anchor.

The skill’s visual diagnosis now directly determines the proposal: preserve the replicated static `1.7` controller and add only a small, explicitly bounded target-bearing trend lead. This uses the existing normalized temporal target signal—not local flow, moments, coordinates, or time—and is meant to ease steering when bearing is already converging while reinforcing it when the wake makes bearing diverge. I’m recording that hypothesis in the required notes before editing the candidate.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. The new lesson treats the three identical `1.7` results as deterministic replay evidence—not wake-phase robustness—and uses that satisfied repeat boundary to permit exactly one bounded target-relative temporal test. I’m invoking the prescribed checker now: guidance semantics first, then the lightweight Julia contract/schema check, then the solver boundary check; no CFD will be run.

The first check exposed a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, so the checker cannot identify exactly one parent. This is the same duplicate-marker condition documented in inherited workers; I’m removing only the duplicate line, then rerunning the guidance check.

The guidance check passes. The prescribed Julia contract could not execute because this workspace has no `julia` binary (exit 127); the candidate file was never truncated. I’ll still complete the checker’s deterministic schema/boundary coverage using the supplied Python guards and a static `params.FIELD` audit, then report the unavailable runtime distinctly from actual failures.

Produced exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:9) adds a quarter-period windowed-bearing lead, bounded to ±2°, while preserving the replicated gain-`1.7` gait.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:44) now distinguishes deterministic snapshot replay from wake-phase robustness and defines the next-axis boundary.

Guidance, parameter-schema, and solver-boundary checks pass. The Julia runtime check was unavailable because `julia` is not installed; no CFD was run. I also removed the duplicate assigned-parent marker from `README.md` so the mandated guidance checker could resolve the parent.
